_doc: The test that proves each shipped feature works. Read by feature_matrix.py.
Keyed by FEATURE, with the pin that currently carries it, and NOT the other
way round. When upstream absorbs a feature the pin is deleted, and deleting
the check with it would put the blind spot back somewhere else: the feature
is still in the release, it just arrives through the base tag now. So an
entry outlives its `owner`, and `owner` becomes null rather than the entry
being removed.
This is the half that cannot be derived. pin_contract.py reads a pin's own
diff and proves the merge kept it, which needs no upkeep but can only ever
prove the MERGE lost nothing -- a regression inside the pin regenerates a
smaller contract that passes. What a feature has to DO is a human sentence.
Every pin in pr-set.json must appear in `features` or in `unchecked`. The
lint enforces that, so adding a pin forces a decision instead of a silence.
`unchecked` is a recorded reason, not a hole.
kinds:
arch        test-llama-archs -a <arch>          builds a synthetic model of
the architecture, decodes 128
tokens on every device and
compares against CPU
backend-op  test-backend-ops test -o <OP>       runs the op against the CPU
reference implementation
mtmd        test-mtmd-impl                      projector registry, no model
A probe that exits 0 having run nothing is a failure, not a pass: both
harnesses do exactly that for an excluded arch or a misspelled op name.
feature_matrix.py rejects skip markers and requires a non-zero case count.
No runner in the prebuild pipeline has a GPU, so the nightly runs this on
CPU and every backend-op check is DEFERRED there: named and counted, never
reported as passing. The kernels are exactly where a merge goes wrong
silently, so before accepting a carry PR that touches one, build it on a
GPU box and run:
python3 scripts/unsloth/feature_matrix.py --build-dir build --gpu
and paste the output into the PR. That is the only place those checks run.

unchecked.unslothai#95: sampling penalties indexed by token id; behaviour is covered by test-sampling, and there is no feature surface of its own to probe
unchecked.unslothai#149: once-per-process HIP warning when GGML_CUDA_ENABLE_UNIFIED_MEMORY is on (=0 parsing is upstream since ggml-org#30327); needs a HIP host, and no runner in the pipeline has one
unchecked.unslothai#157: cudaMemcpyDefault in the ggml_cuda_cpy 2D fast path; needs a CUDA host
unchecked.unslothai#328: Vulkan top_k on a view off minStorageBufferOffsetAlignment (backend draft sampling over an odd vocab); covered by test-backend-ops TOP_K row cases, which need a Vulkan device, and no runner in the pipeline has one
unchecked.unslothai#348: Metal NVFP4 mul_mv, mul_mv_ext, mul_mv_id, mul_mv_mma, mul_mm, mul_mm_id and get_rows kernels; covered by test-backend-ops MUL_MAT, MUL_MAT_ID and GET_ROWS with -p nvfp4, which need a Metal device, and no runner in the pipeline has one. A backend-op check here would pass on CUDA, which has NVFP4 upstream, and so cannot tell the pin apart
unchecked.unslothai#335: backend sampling chains of inactive sequences are flagged as outputs so the graph allocator cannot alias their buffers; only observable with a block draft (DFlash / DSpark) on a multi-slot server, which needs a draft model and a GPU host the pipeline does not have
unchecked.unslothai#376: Windows only: unmap_fragment releases offloaded weight pages from the working set with VirtualUnlock; needs a Windows host, and no runner in the pipeline has one
unchecked.unslothai#158: ROCm_Host compute buffer type on HIP integrated GPUs; needs a ROCm host
unchecked.unslothai#241: CUDA graph cache keyed by shape with no count cap (tensor split keeps replaying its 2 * n_layers + 1 graphs per device), macOS row prefetch and the F16 glm5-next indexer cache under a quantized -ctk (the NextN draft graph is upstream since ggml-org#29928); the first needs a CUDA host (multi-GPU for the cap), the second has no observable output difference, the last needs a real GLM-5-Next model
unchecked.unslothai#243: glm5-next compute buffer size; a memory-layout change with no observable output difference, and the size only shows on a CUDA host with a GLM-5-Next model
unchecked.unslothai#251: --moe-cache-mib auto sizes the ggml-org#29887 MoE expert cache from the fit; it only acts when a MoE model spills on a single GPU, the flag is off by default, and no runner in the pipeline has a GPU
unchecked.unslothai#266: MADV_POPULATE_READ on the non-lazy ranges when MAP_POPULATE is skipped; a page-fault and load-time change with no observable output difference, so there is no feature surface to probe
unchecked.unslothai#311: harmony-xml parser ends a Beam analysis message on <|constrain|> header variants; covered by test-chat, and there is no feature surface of its own to probe
unchecked.unslothai#405: Inkling 2 DSpark draft (ggml-org#32218 at 0a9105de4, frozen for the published padded-vocab drafters) (DFLASH arch with the Inkling 2 backbone and recurrent Markov head); test-llama-archs has no DFlash case because a draft needs a target context, and an end-to-end check needs the Inkling-2-Small DSpark draft GGUF and a GPU host the pipeline does not have
unchecked.unslothai#395: earlier looped inkling2 layout loaded as inkling2_loop; the legacy looped config in test-llama-archs runs in the CPU gate build, and an end-to-end check needs a looped GGUF the pipeline does not have
unchecked.unslothai#396: looped layers placed by the layers that hold weights, with per-visit host weight views; it only differs with partial offload or several GPUs on a looped GGUF, which the pipeline does not have
unchecked.unslothai#397: llama-quantize keeps the DSpark fuse weights F32; needs a DSpark draft GGUF the pipeline does not have
unchecked.unslothai#385: Inkling 2 attention chunked over query rows once the dense relative bias for a full cache passes 2^29 elements; it only engages with a large context window (a cache above about 21K cells at -ub 512 for 48 heads), which the small synthetic test-llama-archs context never reaches, and below that budget the graph is unchanged
